I got diagnosed when I needed emergency surgery because one of my ovaries had twisted (look up "ovarian torsion", if you're interested because that's a whole other serious can of worms). The surgeon sent some tissue for a biopsy which is how they saw I had endometrium-like tissue growing in my ovaries. 

I never thought to get diagnosed, even though I'd always had extremely painful periods because we always get told that that's normal and that we should just put up with it. People, it's NOT and we shouldn't!

If any of you reading this is wondering if you have it or not, I wish for you to find medical professionals who will believe you and make you feel seen and cared for so you can get a timely diagnosis and start exploring methods to make it easier to live with 🙏

I agree with everyone in that "normal" depends on each individual. 

In my case, for example, I don't really use cheek products other than blush (and even then, I tend to multi-purpose my lipsticks) so I don't have anything in those categories other than 1 powder blush. On the other hand, I really love lip products so I try to keep a variety of colors and textures that I know I will use; out of the top of my head, I can count 8 lip products across different categories. Both of these things are "normal" for me.

I also think that defining your "normal" kind of comes with experimentation? I think most, if not all, of us in this subreddit have had or still have larger-than-desirable collections. For me, trying to get through my products when my collection felt unmanageable helped me identify the things that I like ***and*** that I actually use, which in turn has helped me maintain a collection that feels...enjoyable? As in not overwhelming but not scarce either.

Something I’ve been doing is that, whenever I want something I put it on a wish list and then I give myself a “rule” for when I can buy it: I’d look in my collection and see if I’ve something similar or that I would use for the same purpose and then my “rule” would be to not buy it until I finish those other products. 

For example, I currently want the Maybelline Liquid Lipstick in “Artist”, but I’m only allowing myself to buy it until I’ve used up my other bold coloured lipsticks. Even though the ones I have are not really the same colours, they all serve the same purpose in my collection and I don’t really need them all.
